messages:
jonathan: Quick follow-up after the autoscale RFC — thinking about SLA-tiering + admission boundary with operator. TL;DR: can we keep runtime responsibility limited to admission decisions while operator owns long-term provisioning? Thoughts?

mia: +1. I prefer runtime to only make ephemeral admission decisions. Operator should own headroom budgeting and cross-tenant accounting. Main pain: warmup/credits need cross-component agreement.

elaine: FWIW I sketched an API where operator exposes `ReserveHeadroom(tenant, amount_ms)` and returns a token you consume. Runtime calls this for burst admits. Race happens when operator lags — requests pile and tokens arrive late.

sam: What if runtime keeps an optimistic local cache of tokens with soft expiry and reconciliation? Avoids blocking tail latency for the fast path.

jonathan: Optimistic cache is attractive but risk is overcommit/cost spikes. We need a concrete safety cap so runtime can't exhaust operator budget.

mia: Agreed. Proposal: define a `safety_fraction` per SLA tier. Runtime can admit optimistically up to that fraction, then must synchronously call `ReserveHeadroom`. Also emit telemetry: `optimistic_admits`, `optimistic_overflow`.

orch-bot: deploy-check: autoscale-proto-v2 rolled to canary (env=staging). 2/5 healthchecks failing on scale-down window. Link: https://ci.redwood/in/1234 :warning:

elaine: On eviction semantics — prefer to evict preemptible/burst nodes first and backfill from reserve. Important: tenant billing needs transparent tags so we don't misattribute optimistic cost.

sam: Sketch of admission flow we can implement in runtime:
```
if local_cache.has(token) then admit
else if optimistic_count < safety_limit then admit and mark optimistic
else call operator.ReserveHeadroom sync
```
Mark optimistic admits with `optimistic=true` tag for reconciliation.

mia: Rollout plan suggestion:
1) Enable optimistic cache only for LOW priority SLA for 2 weeks.
2) Collect metrics + alerts on `optimistic_evictions` and `optimistic_reconciliations`.
3) If stable, expand to MED priority with lower `safety_fraction`.

jonathan: Question: operator unresponsive scenarios — what should runtime do? Auto-fallback to cheaper/quantized model variant, queue, or serve 429? Need deterministic behavior per tenant.

elaine: Propose a fallback ladder configurable per-tenant: cached-token -> optimistic -> operator-sync -> model-variant-fallback -> 429. That way critical tenants can prefer variant-fallback over hard errors.

sam: Also ensure every optimistic admit carries `request_origin=runtime_optimistic_v1` tag so billing and cost reports can split optimistic vs operator-confirmed usage. Reconciliation job consumes tokens and marks records.

jonathan: OK action items: @mia add `safety_fraction` + optimistic metric names to the autoscale RFC; @elaine update operator `ReserveHeadroom` API doc with token semantics and timeout; @sam prototype local-cache TTL + reconciliation loop (staging only). I'll schedule a 30m sync to finalize thresholds.

mia: Will add RFC patch this afternoon. Staging canary is good place to validate metrics. :+1:

elaine: I'll update API doc and include example error codes for timeouts (409 = operator busy, 504 = operator timed out).

sam: I'll push a small runtime PR with the cache implementation and a feature flag.

jonathan: Thanks — meeting invite incoming.
